tasks.title: cli: the argument parser and the two renderings

details.goal: One parser for both surfaces and one place that decides TOON vs JSON, so the CLI and the MCP answer cannot disagree about the bytes of an envelope.
details.contract:
Port src/shared/cli/args.ts (473 lines) and src/shared/cli/render.ts (60 lines).
Two parsers, both from the same field descriptors:
- tool calls, whose declared fields come from the seven manifests and whose undeclared keys are dropped (src/index.ts:1092-1106 shows the current behaviour);
- verb calls, which take their own flag set and REFUSE a flag that is not in it, with exit 2. The verb flag table is data in this module and must cover every flag the TypeScript CLI accepts today (src/index.ts:1399, 1440-1447, bin/sangkar.ts:60-90): worker takes --mode full|fast and --force; index adds --yes and --no-register; telemetry takes --out, --serve, --port, --host, --since; daemon takes a subcommand plus --port and --host (run only); repo takes a subcommand, a path, --watch, --watch-interval and --telemetry. Every verb also accepts the four globals.
Parser grammar, exactly: --k v and --k=v; --no-<bool> negation; a bare boolean flag means true; --k true|false accepted only for booleans; repeated array flags collect; integer-array items split on : (--range 1:5); a single positional binds the only required string field; a flag-prefixed token is never a value. Globals: --repo-root <path>, --data-dir <path>, --json, --help|-h; split_globals removes them and reports them, resolve_command finds the verb with globals on either side.
A wrong type, a missing required field, a refused key or a malformed value produces a usage error carrying that verb's or tool's usage block; usage_of renders the same block as the TypeScript side, including the clamp notes.
Renderer: render_json gives compact JSON plus a trailing newline; render_toon gives the encoder from TASK-010 plus a trailing newline; render_output picks between them; mcp_text gives the same without the trailing newline; exit_code_of returns 0 unless the status is Error or Bootstrapping (then 1). EXIT_FAILURE = 1, EXIT_USAGE = 2.
Tests: every case of tests/cli-args.test.ts and tests/cli-render.test.ts, plus one case per verb flag including --yes on index and its refusal on worker.
steps: Port the parser with the `InputLiteral`/`InputField` descriptors from the manifests (TASK-027..033 supply the data).
Port `usage_of` including the clamp annotations.
Wire the renderer to TASK-010's decided encoder and keep JSON byte-identical.
Write the tests, including one asserting `render_json` output equals `src/index.ts`'s `JSON.stringify(envelope)` for the same fixture.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-cli --test args_render` exits 0.
Done when: `--range 1:5` parses to `[1,5]`, `--json` after the verb is accepted, and a JSON rendering of the `status` golden is byte-identical to the golden's `stdout` when the golden was captured with `--json`.

details.goal: The trust tool: is the graph current, what does it cover, and what can it not see — with the repository identity and the health block.
details.contract:
Port `src/tools/status/manifest.ts` + `handler.ts` (602 lines).
Name `status`; description first sentence VERBATIM: `Report whether the graph is current and what it covers.`; parameters: `paths: array<string>` (default `[]`), `budget: integer` (default 800), `repo: string` (no default).
Payload top-level keys, in this order: `project{name,root,branch,remote,commit,db_path}`, `config{source:"project"|"global"}`, `graph{nodes,edges,size_bytes,db_path}`, `unresolved{total,material,buckets}`, `languages[]`, `paths[]`, `health{indexer,last_publish_ms,consecutive_failures,statement_cache_entries}`. `payload` is `null` for `bootstrapping` and `error`.
Handler pattern (the same in all seven): read meta -> generation guard (an empty graph is `bootstrapping`, not an error) -> build `argsHash` = `sha256:` + hex of the compact JSON of `{budget, paths}` -> verify an incoming `cursor` BEFORE reading -> assemble -> `ok(...)` -> `emit(env, budget, mint)` -> if `budget_floor_of(emitted) > budget` then `fail("budget_too_large")`. `mint` returns the raw `position`.

details.goal: The core query: what is connected to one symbol — callers, callees, implementers, importers, tests — with an honest ambiguity answer and bucket filtering.
details.contract:
Port `src/tools/trace/manifest.ts` + `handler.ts` (1193 lines, the largest handler).
Name `trace`; description first sentence VERBATIM: `Show what is connected to one symbol: callers, callees, implementers, importers and tests.`; parameters: `query: string` REQUIRED, `direction: enum[all,in,out]` (default `all`), `kinds: array<enum[file,module,class,function,method,test,endpoint]>`, `path: string`, `depth: integer` (default 2, min 1, max 4), `budget: integer` (default 3200), `unresolved: enum[builtin_stdlib,external_package,internal_module,dynamic_property_call,receiver_type_unknown,ambiguous]`, `cursor: string`, `repo: string`.

`argsHash` = `sha256:` + hex over the compact JSON of `{query,direction,kinds,path,unresolved,depth,budget}` in that key order. `mint` position = `start + entries.len()` of what was actually shown, so a resumed page never repeats or skips an item.
The `unresolved` filter is applied to the census rows AFTER bucketing, and the filtered rows are what the payload lists; `unresolved_census` stays the full census.

tasks.title: tool: index, spawning the worker named by config

details.goal: The repair tool: start a full or fast index run, map the worker's exit status onto an envelope, and — during the migration — be able to start the TypeScript worker until phase_3 lands.
details.contract:
Port `src/tools/index/manifest.ts` + `handler.ts` (648 lines).
Name `index`; description first sentence VERBATIM: `Admin: force a full or fast index, or repair a broken one.`; parameters: `force: boolean` (default false), `mode: enum[full,fast]` (default full), `repo: string`, `register: boolean` (default true).
Payload: `{mode, duration_ms, previous_generation, files{indexed,parsed,failed,skipped}}`; no list, so `emit` is called with a mint that panics if reached (the TypeScript side uses `unreachableMint`).
Worker invocation: `ctx.config.worker_cmd` + `worker --repo-root <root> --data-dir <dir>` (+ `--force`/`--mode` when set). During the migration `worker_cmd` may be `["bun", "bin/sangkar.ts"]`; after phase_3 it is `[current_exe]`. Never read the environment in the handler.
Exit-status mapping: `0` -> `ok` with the counts parsed from the worker's stderr JSON lines; `2` -> `ok` with zero files and a summary saying nothing changed; `75` -> `error` code `index_locked` with `retryable: true`; `1` or a signal -> `error` code `internal` carrying the worker's last stderr line as `detail`; a spawn failure -> `error` code `internal` naming the failed command.
`register: true` registers the repository in `<home>/sangkar.json` after a successful run, through `sangkar_core::registry`.
Tests port `tests/tools-index.test.ts` using a fake worker script (a shell script that prints two JSON lines and exits with the code under test), covering all five outcomes.

Port the spawn with piped stderr, a line reader and a timeout.
Port the exit-status mapping and the count parsing.
Port registration on success and the unreachable mint.
Write tests/index.rs driving a fake worker for 0, 1, 2, 75 and a spawn error.

`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-tools --test index` exits 0 with five cases.

tasks.title: cli: verb dispatch and the tool registry

details.goal: The process entry point as bin/sangkar.ts is today: six reserved verbs, every other token a tool name, globals accepted on either side, usage on stderr with exit 2 — plus the fixed-order tool registry it dispatches to.
details.contract:
Port `bin/sangkar.ts` (180 lines) and `src/index.ts`'s composition half.
Verb set, exactly six: `mcp`, `worker`, `index`, `telemetry`, `daemon`, `repo`. Any other first non-global token is a tool name; no token at all means `mcp`. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` failure (an error or bootstrapping envelope, a refused store, a daemon start/stop failure, `repo remove` on an unregistered path), `2` usage (unknown verb, bad flag, repo-selection refusal, index-gate refusal). Exit code `70` has no producer in this binary — the missing-interpreter preflight it existed for is gone; it survives only in the npm launcher shim (TASK-058) for a missing platform package.
`sangkar-tools::registry` holds `TOOLS: [RegisteredTool; 7]` in the documented order (status, summary, trace, search, impact, expand, index) mapping name to descriptor to handler, with the descriptor derived from each manifest exactly as `src/index.ts:227-275` derives it: an object schema with properties, an optional required list and an optional examples list. Registration is an explicit list, never discovery.
`dispatch.rs` wires the six verbs to their modules (mcp to TASK-035, telemetry to TASK-054, daemon to TASK-056, repo to TASK-071, index to TASK-072's gate plus the spawn) and the tool names to the registry, and owns the composition root: build `AppConfig`, open the store through TASK-070, build `ToolContext`, route the envelope (TASK-035), render (TASK-026), exit.
Usage text goes to stderr, never stdout; the repo usage block it prints is copied verbatim from `bin/sangkar.ts:79-90`.
Tests: verb resolution with globals before and after the verb, the six reserved names each reaching their module, an unknown verb's exit 2 plus a stderr usage block, a tool name resolving to the registry, and no stdout bytes for any failure path.

Add `sangkar-tools/src/registry.rs` with the fixed-order table and the descriptor derivation.
Wire the six verbs to their modules and the tool names to the registry.
Map errors to exit codes 1 and 2, with no 70 path in this binary.
Write tests/dispatch.rs over a fake argv.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-cli --test dispatch` exits 0.
Done when: `sangkar bogus` exits 2 with the usage block on stderr and nothing on stdout, the registry order matches the golden tools/list order, and no exit code 70 remains in `rust/crates/sangkar-cli/src`.

tasks.title: cli: the MCP server, route() post-conditions, in-band errors

details.goal: The stdio server: two handlers only, results framed as one text block, every error in-band, and the post-conditions the composition root applies to every envelope before it leaves.
details.contract:
Transport: the decision from TASK-011 (rmcp over newline-delimited JSON-RPC, or the hand-rolled frame). Server options: name `sangkar`, `server_version()`, capabilities `{tools:{}}`, and `instructions: INSTRUCTIONS_TEXT`.
Handlers: `tools/list` -> `[descriptor]` from TASK-034's registry; `tools/call` -> `CallToolResult { content: [{type:"text", text: mcp_text(envelope, output_json)}], is_error }` with NO `structuredContent`, `output_json` from the `--json` global, `is_error = status in {error, bootstrapping}`. An unknown tool, a bad argument, a cursor refusal, a budget refusal and a handler panic ALL become a text envelope with `status: error` — never a JSON-RPC error.
`route.rs` post-conditions, applied after every handler: `next_tools` is always replaced by `next_tools_for(tool)`; a `root_mismatch` staleness forces `read_status.stale = true` with its reason; `decisive = !stale`. A handler that throws becomes `fail(...)` built from `boundary_spec(store, tool, "<tool> could not answer", "the call failed before the graph answered")` with `UNKNOWN_COVERAGE {complete:false}` and an `unchecked_read_status`.
Shutdown: SIGINT/SIGTERM drain in-flight calls, then exit 0; stdin EOF is the client-gone signal. Nothing writes to stdout except the protocol.
Tests: replay `rust/tests/vectors/mcp_session.ndjson` and compare `tools/list` against the TypeScript descriptor JSON captured in `mcp_session_ts_only.json`; assert an invalid argument yields `isError: true` with a `cursor_invalid`-style envelope rather than a protocol error; assert a panicking handler yields code `internal`; assert stdout has exactly one JSON object per response and no other bytes.
steps: Wire the transport from TASK-011's decision with the two handlers.
Implement `route.rs`'s three post-conditions.
Implement the throw boundary and the two failure envelopes.
Wire signal handling and stdin EOF.
Write tests/mcp_surface.rs against the recorded session.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-cli --test mcp_surface` exits 0.
Done when: the replayed `tools/list` equals the TypeScript capture field by field, and a test asserts zero non-protocol bytes on stdout for a full session.

tasks.title: core: process facts for telemetry and the worker default

details.goal: The four process facts that used to come from Bun — version, os, arch, own executable — so telemetry records and the worker's default command stop depending on an interpreter.
details.contract:
```rust
pub fn server_version() -> &'static str;      // env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")
pub fn runtime_version() -> String;           // `rustc <version>`, captured at build time
pub fn os() -> &'static str;                  // std::env::consts::OS
pub fn arch() -> &'static str;                // std::env::consts::ARCH
pub fn current_exe() -> std::io::Result<PathBuf>;
pub fn git_available() -> bool;
```
This module replaces `src/shared/runtime.ts` (77 lines), of which only the facts survive: the Bun version gate disappears with the interpreter, so this binary has no exit code 70 (the npm launcher shim keeps 70 for a missing platform package — say that in the module comment). `runtime_version()` feeds the telemetry field `bun_version`, which KEEPS its name for record-shape compatibility because the report never reads it (`src/shared/telemetry/report.ts:277-311`).

details.goal: sangkar repo add|remove|list|config must keep working: it is how a user registers the trees the daemon then watches.
details.contract:
Port `src/shared/cli/repo.ts` (332 lines).
Subcommands: `add <path>`, `remove <path>`, `list`, `config <path> [--watch t|f] [--watch-interval ms] [--telemetry t|f]`.
Rules: `~/` is expanded; a positional that starts with a flag dash is refused (the first non-flag token is the path, `repo.ts:16`); `--watch-interval` outside 1000..=300000 is a usage refusal with exit 2; `config` resolves the tree the same way a tool call does (a named path, else cwd autodetection) and writes `<dataDir>/config.json` through `sangkar_core::repo_config`, reporting the file it wrote; `add`/`remove` go through `sangkar_core::registry` and are idempotent.
stdout lines, verbatim: `registered <path>`, `already registered <path>`, `removed <path>`, `not registered <path>`, and for `config`/`list` the `watch=on|off`, `interval=<n>ms`, `telemetry=on|off` lines; `list --json` prints the registry document `{"version":1,"repos":[...]}`.
Exit codes: `1` for `remove` on an unregistered path, `2` for a usage refusal, `0` otherwise.
Tests port the CLI-facing half of `tests/repo-config.test.ts`: add twice, remove a registered and an unregistered path, `list` plain and with `--json`, a `config` write followed by a read, the interval clamps refused at 999 and 300001, and a dash-prefixed positional refused.
steps: Port the subcommand parser and the tilde expansion.
Port add/remove/list over the registry module.
Port config over the repo-config module, including the clamp refusals.
Port the stdout lines and exit codes.
Write the tests over a temp home and temp trees.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-cli --test repo_cmd` exits 0.
Done when: `repo add` is idempotent (second run prints `already registered`), `list --json` parses as the registry document, and `--watch-interval 999` exits 2.
